The literal path /kaggle/input must therefore show exactly this stage's inputs while the stage runs: e.g. a container with the virtual input mounted at /kaggle/input (as release/docker/ff.py does; FF_LITERAL_KAGGLE=mounted), or a symlink /kaggle/input -> the virtual input on a Linux host without /kaggle (the runner makes it when this flag is set). In a Kaggle notebook whose own /kaggle/input holds other attachments, run this stage in a session with exactly its inputs attached (as the original run); the runner can only warn there (FF_LITERAL_STRICT=1 makes it an error). /kaggle/input must also hold no second copy of the files these modules look for (e.g. an original saved copy of an artifact rebuilt in the session): they take the first hit of their own scan. Same wording as stages/50_eval/e112f1sx (WP-G), which carries the same modules.
